heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Armenia
heroData.subtitle: Hire without a local entity
heroData.description: Establish a presence in Armenia quickly using Employer of Record services.
heroData.bestFor: Companies testing the market or hiring remote talent

steps.title: Provider Selection
steps.description: Choose an EOR provider with a local entity in Armenia. Evaluate based on fees (typically $200-$600/month or % of salary), compliance record, and technology platform (HRIS integration).

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: The EOR drafts a compliant employment contract under Armenian Labor Code. Contracts must represent the local currency (AMD), working hours (40h/week), and mandatory benefits.

steps.title: Employee Registration
steps.description: The EOR registers the employee with tax authorities and social security. Employee must provide ID, social security card, and other personal banking details.

steps.title: Onboarding & Payroll Setup
steps.description: Employee is onboarded into the EOR's payroll system. First month's salary and deposit (if required) are processed. Tax code application is verified.

items.title: Permanent Establishment (PE) Risk
items.text: Using an EOR for extended periods (18-24+ months) for senior sales or management roles may trigger PE risks, potentially subjecting the foreign parent company to Armenian corporate tax.

items.title: Termination Rules
items.text: Armenia is not an 'at-will' employment jurisdiction. Termination requires valid grounds (redundancy, performance, misconduct) and strictly regulated notice periods (14-60 days based on tenure).

items.title: Probation Period
items.text: Standard probation period is up to 3 months. In specific cases, it can be extended to 6 months. Termination during probation is simpler, requiring 3 days' notice.

items.title: Working Hours
items.text: Standard work week is 40 hours (5 days x 8 hours). Overtime is capped at 4 hours per 2 consecutive days or 180 hours per year, paid at 150%.

items.title: Leave Entitlements
items.text: Minimum annual leave is 20 working days (for 5-day week) or 24 working days (for 6-day week). 12 public holidays are observed.

items.title: 13th Month Salary
items.text: Not mandatory by law, but some international and tech companies offer it as a bonus.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors via EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, many EORs offer 'Agent of Record' services for contractors. However, ensure verified contractor status to avoid misclassification risks.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle IP transfer?
faqs.answer: Yes, compliant employment contracts drafted by the EOR include strong IP assignment clauses ensuring all work product belongs to the client.

faqs.question: What happens if I want to hire the employee directly later?
faqs.answer: Most EOR contracts include a 'conversion' clause. You may need to pay a conversion fee (e.g., $2,000 or 1 month salary) to transfer the employee to your own Armenian entity.

steps.title: Data Collection
steps.description: Gather attendance records, overtime hours, bonuses, and sick leave data (80% pay for first 5 days) by the 25th-30th of the current month.

steps.title: Calculation
steps.description: Calculate gross-to-net salary. Deduct PIT (20%), Pension contribution (5-10%), and Military Stamp Duty (1,500-15,000 AMD). Apply employer social payments.

steps.title: Tax Filing
steps.description: Submit monthly income tax return to State Revenue Committee by the 20th of the following month. Remit withheld taxes and social contributions.

steps.title: Salary Disbursement
steps.description: Pay net salaries to employees. Payment must be made in AMD to local bank accounts. Pay slips should be issued electronically or physically.

items.title: Sick Pay
items.text: First 5 days paid by employer at 80%. Remaining days paid by state. Medical certificate required.

items.title: Maternity Leave
items.text: 140 days (70 prenatal + 70 postnatal). Paid at 100% of average salary, reimbursed by the state up to a cap.

items.title: Private Health Insurance
items.text: Not mandatory yet (universal rollout started 2025), but highly expected by tech talent. Typical cost $300-$600/year/employee.

items.title: Military Stamp Duty Tiers
items.text: Fixed monthly fee: 1,500 AMD (up to 100k salary), 3,000 AMD (100k-200k), 5,500 AMD (200k-500k), 8,500 AMD (500k-1M), 15,000 AMD (>1M). Rates simplified Dec 2025.

items.title: Sick Leave Rules
items.text: Employer pays first 5 working days at 80% of average salary. From day 6, the state pays. Total sick leave max 120 consecutive days or 140 days/year.

items.title: IT Startups Tax Benefit
items.text: Certified IT startups may benefit from a reduced Income Tax rate of 10% for employees (instead of 20%), subject to specific certification by the Ministry of High-Tech Industry.

items.title: Digital Payments Mandatory
items.text: Employers with 10+ employees must pay salaries via bank transfer. Cash payments are restricted and require specific written requests.

items.title: E-Contract Platform
items.text: Voluntary adoption of the unified government e-contract platform begins in 2025. Mandatory for all new contracts from Jan 1, 2026.

items.title: Severance Pay
items.text: Redundancy severance is 1 month's average salary. Long-term disability/age retirement severance scales with tenure (up to 44 days for 15+ years).

steps.title: Notice Period
steps.description: Provide written notice 14-60 days in advance, depending on tenure. 14 days for <1 year, 60 days for >10 years.

steps.title: Final Calculation
steps.description: Calculate unpaid wages and unused annual leave compensation. Calculate severance if applicable (redundancy).

steps.title: Final Payment
steps.description: Must be paid on the last working day. Any delay incurs a penalty of 0.15% per day.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum wage?
faqs.answer: Yes, as of 2025, the minimum monthly wage is 75,000 AMD (approx. $190).

faqs.question: How is overtime calculated?
faqs.answer: Overtime is paid at a premium of 50% on top of the hourly rate. Night work (10 PM - 6 AM) carries a 30% premium.

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, bonuses and allowances are generally treated as part of gross income and subject to the standard 20% PIT and pension contributions.

items.title: Pension Formula
items.text: If salary > 500k: (Salary * 10%) - 25,000 AMD. Max contribution 87,500 AMD.

items.title: Flat Tax
items.text: Income tax is a flat 20% on gross income.

steps.title: Identify Gross Amount
steps.description: Ensure amount is Gross, not Cost to Company.

steps.title: Apply Pension
steps.description: Check if employee was born after 1974 (mandatory).

steps.title: Deduct Stamp Duty
steps.description: Apply fixed tier based on salary range.

items.title: Employer Burden
items.text: Standard employer social payments are low, but total cost includes sick leave risk (first 5 days) and administrative overhead.

items.title: IT Certificate Impact
items.text: With IT certificate, employer avoids standard income tax gross-up pressure as employees pay only 10% PIT (vs 20%).

faqs.question: How accurate is this?
faqs.answer: Estimates based on standard 2025 rates. Health insurance (2025 rollout) may add ~4-10k AMD.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Armenia
heroData.subtitle: Fast, Digital, Foreign-Friendly
heroData.description: Register a Limited Liability Company (LLC) in Armenia with 100% foreign ownership allowed.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Check company name availability via State Register. Avoid restricted words like 'Armenia' unless you pay the annual fee (600,000 AMD).

steps.title: Document Preparation
steps.description: Prepare Articles of Incorporation, Shareholder Resolution, and passport translations. Foreign corporate shareholders need apostilled extracts.

steps.title: Registration Submission
steps.description: Submit documents to the State Register Agency of Legal Entities (e-register.am). Can be done in-person or remotely with PoA.

steps.title: Tax & Bank Setup
steps.description: Obtain Tax ID (TIN) immediately upon registration. Open a corporate bank account (requires in-person visit or strong PoA). Submit UBO declaration within 40 days.

items.title: Limited Liability Company (LLC)
items.text: Most popular form. No minimum capital requirement (1 AMD suffices). Shareholders not liable for debts beyond investment.

items.title: Joint Stock Company (JSC)
items.text: Can be Open (OJSC) or Closed (CJSC). Closed JSCs limited to 49 shareholders. Suitable for larger investments.

items.title: IT Sector Incentives
items.text: Armenia offers a 0% Corporate Income Tax incentive for certified IT startups, though recent changes moved some to a special turnover tax regime.

items.title: Enhanced Due Diligence
items.text: Non-resident companies face strict KYC/AML checks. Approvals can take 10-21 days compared to 3-7 days for locals.

items.title: Sanctions Screening
items.text: Businesses with potential ties to sanctioned entities (even indirect) face extended scrutiny. Clear documentation of funds is non-negotiable.

items.title: Remote Opening
items.text: While possible via Power of Attorney, remote bank account opening is difficult. In-person visits significantly improve success rates.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner own 100% of an Armenian company?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is fully permitted. No local director is required.

faqs.question: Do I need to visit Armenia?
faqs.answer: No, incorporation can be done remotely via Power of Attorney. However, bank account opening is difficult without a physical presence.

faqs.question: What is the UBO declaration?
faqs.answer: All companies must declare their Ultimate Beneficial Owners (individuals owning 20%+) to the State Register within 40 days of incorporation.

heroData.title: Talent Acquisition in Armenia
heroData.subtitle: Access Tech Talent & Skilled Workforce
heroData.description: Recruit top talent in Armenia, known for its strong IT and engineering sectors.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Utilize local job boards (Staff.am, JobFinder.am), LinkedIn, and agencies. Focus on Yerevan for tech talent.

steps.title: Screening & Interview
steps.description: Conduct technical screenings. Armenian candidates often have strong English and Russian language skills.

steps.title: Offer & Negotiation
steps.description: Salaries are typically quoted net in AMD or USD (paid in AMD). Be prepared to discuss benefits like health insurance and training.

items.title: Tech Talent Hub
items.text: Armenia is a regional tech hub ('Silicon Mountain'). Strong pool of developers, engineers, and AI specialists.

items.title: Agency Fees
items.text: Recruitment agency fees typically range from 10% to 20% of the candidate's first annual gross salary.

items.title: Digital Nomad Visa
items.text: While not a specific 'visa', Armenia allows 180-day visa-free stay for many nations, attracting remote workers. Residency permits are available for longer stays.

items.title: Remote Work Adoption
items.text: Over 70% of Armenian tech companies offer hybrid or fully remote work options to attract senior talent.

items.title: Tanger
items.text: Established generalist agency operating since 2000.

items.title: DevsData & Meettal
items.text: Specialized agencies for IT and tech recruitment.

items.title: AtoZ Serwis Plus
items.text: International agency assisting with cross-border staffing.

faqs.question: Where should I post jobs?
faqs.answer: Staff.am is the leading platform for white-collar and tech jobs. LinkedIn is also widely used.

faqs.question: What are common benefits?
faqs.answer: Private health insurance (as state coverage is limited), gym memberships, and educational stipends are common in the tech sector.

heroData.title: HRIS Solutions in Armenia
heroData.subtitle: Manage Workforce Data
heroData.description: Software for payroll, attendance, and employee management in Armenia.

items.title: Local Providers
items.text: ArmSoft (Armenian Software) is a dominant local player for accounting and payroll, often integrated with HR modules.

items.title: New Entrants
items.text: Smart HR Software and Mawared HR are emerging options for SMEs.

items.title: Global Platforms
items.text: Global platforms like Deel, Remote, and Rippling work well for international teams but requires checks for local statutory reporting features.

steps.title: Needs Assessment
steps.description: Determine if you need deep local compliance (tax reporting) or just global workforce visibility.

steps.title: Vendor Selection
steps.description: Evaluate ArmSoft for local compliance vs. global tools for UX. Check for Armenian language support if needed for local staff.

steps.title: Migration
steps.description: Import employee data, specifically tax IDs and social security numbers.

items.title: ArmSoft
items.text: Standard for finance and payroll in Armenia. Heavy UI but compliant.

items.title: BambooHR / Workday
items.text: Used by larger multinationals in Armenia, often requiring custom integrations for local payroll.

items.title: Haystack / Teamable
items.text: Armenian-founded HR tech tools often popular in the local tech ecosystem.

faqs.question: Is local data hosting required?
faqs.answer: Armenia's Personal Data Protection Law regulates data processing. While strict localization isn't always enforced like in Russia/China, secure processing is mandatory.

faqs.question: Can I use Excel?
faqs.answer: For very small teams (1-5), yes. But monthly tax reporting complexity makes software highly recommended.

heroData.title: Accounting Services in Armenia
heroData.subtitle: IFRS & Local Compliance
heroData.description: Bookkeeping, financial reporting, and audit services for Armenian entities.

steps.title: Setup
steps.description: Establish Chart of Accounts compliant with Armenian standards (based on IFRS). Setup ArmSoft or cloud accounting.

steps.title: Monthly Bookkeeping
steps.description: Process invoices (e-invoicing is common via e-invoicing.am), bank statements, and expense reports.

steps.title: Tax Returns
steps.description: File VAT, Payroll, and Turnover tax returns monthly/quarterly.

steps.title: Annual Closing
steps.description: Prepare annual financial statements. CIT return due by April 20.

items.title: IFRS Adoption
items.text: Armenia has fully adopted IFRS. Banks and large entities must use full IFRS. SMEs may use IFRS for SMEs.

items.title: Mandatory Audit
items.text: Audits are mandatory for large entities (Assets > 3B AMD, Revenue > 4B AMD, or >100 employees) and public interest entities.

items.title: E-Invoicing
items.text: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for VAT payers. The 'e-Invoicing' system of the State Revenue Committee is robust.

items.title: Direct Integration
items.text: ArmSoft offers direct integration with major Armenian banks (Ameriabank, ACBA) for payment processing and statement imports.

items.title: Excel Export/Import
items.text: Most banks support .xml or .csv export formats compatible with local accounting software, reducing manual data entry.

faqs.question: What is the tax year?
faqs.answer: The tax year is the calendar year, Jan 1 to Dec 31.

faqs.question: Can I use Xero/QuickBooks?
faqs.answer: Yes, but local tax filing requires data to be reformatted or bridged to local systems for submission.

steps.title: Jan-Feb
steps.description: Prepare annual financial statements. Re-confirm tax regime elections if applicable.

steps.title: April 20
steps.description: Deadline for Corporate Income Tax (CIT) return.

steps.title: July 1
steps.description: Deadline for UBO declaration updates and submission of annual statistical reports.

items.title: UBO Declaration
items.text: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership must be declared annually. Failure to file incurs fines and banking blocks.

items.title: Cash Restrictions
items.text: Cash transactions between businesses are limited (300k AMD limit). Employee salaries must be paid via bank transfer.

items.title: GDPR / Data Protection
items.text: Law on Protection of Personal Data aligns with GDPR principles. Breaches can lead to fines.

items.title: Late Filing
items.text: Late tax filing incurs fines (usually 5% of tax due every 15 days, capped at 100%).

items.title: Transfer Pricing
items.text: TP rules apply to transactions > 200M AMD/year. Documentation required.

steps.title: Application
steps.description: Director must apply to Ekeng CJSC (e-governance infrastructure provider) for an e-signature card or mobile ID.

steps.title: Verification
steps.description: Requires physical presence or valid PoA. Foreign directors need their passport translated and notarized.

steps.title: Activation
steps.description: Pay annual fee (3,000 AMD). Install software drivers to sign tax returns and legal documents electronically.

faqs.question: Can I keep my books abroad?
faqs.answer: Records must be accessible and available for tax audits in Armenia. Electronic copies usually suffice.

faqs.question: Is a company seal required?
faqs.answer: Since 2011, company seals are voluntary, though some banks still request them.

items.title: IT Sector Regime
items.text: Startups can apply for special IT certification. Previously 0% CIT, now shifting to 1% turnover tax for qualified activities in 2025.

items.title: Micro-Business
items.text: Businesses with revenue < 24M AMD/year may be exempt from CIT and VAT (0% rate), subject to activity exclusions.

items.title: Free Economic Zones
items.text: Companies in FEZs (e.g., Alliance, Meridian) are exempt from CIT, VAT, and property tax.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Company receives TIN upon incorporation. Must elect special tax regime (turnover/micro) within 20 days or default to standard CIT/VAT.

steps.title: Periodic Filings
steps.description: VAT is filed monthly (if >100M AMD turnover) or quarterly. Turnover tax filed quarterly.

steps.title: Annual CIT
steps.description: Corporate Income Tax return must be filed electronically by April 20.

items.title: DTT Network
items.text: Armenia has ~50 Double Taxation Treaties, including with France, Germany, UK, UAE, and China. New treaty with Japan ratified May 2025.

items.title: VAT Refund
items.text: Input VAT exceeding output VAT is refundable monthly. Foreign B2B services (reverse charge) may require specific handling.

items.title: Tax-Free Shopping
items.text: Applies to foreign individuals for non-food goods >100k AMD purchased in designated stores.

faqs.question: Is there double taxation relief?
faqs.answer: Yes, Armenia has Double Taxation Treaties (DTTs) with approx 50 countries.

faqs.question: What is the VAT threshold?
faqs.answer: General VAT threshold is 115 million AMD (approx $290k). Below this, businesses pay Turnover Tax.

heroData.title: M&A and Legal Services
heroData.subtitle: Structuring Deals
heroData.description: Legal frameworks for mergers, acquisitions, and contracts in Armenia.

items.title: Competition Commission
items.text: Mergers must be notified to the Competition Protection Commission (CPC) if combined assets/revenue > 4 Billion AMD.

items.title: Shareholder Rights
items.text: Minority shareholders in JSCs have tag-along/drag-along rights in certain cases. 75%+ acquisition triggers mandatory tender offer.

items.title: Due Diligence
items.text: Crucial to check tax liabilities and UBO history. State Register provides some transparency.

steps.title: Agreement
steps.description: Draft Merger Agreement approved by shareholder meetings of all entities.

steps.title: Creditor Notice
steps.description: Notify creditors. They have 30 days to demand early repayment or guarantees.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Register the new structure with the State Register. Successor entity assumes all rights/obligations.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, Armenia recognizes electronic signatures (e-signature tokens widely used for tax).

faqs.question: Can I force a buyout?
faqs.answer: Squeeze-out rules exist for public JSCs but are less defined for LLCs.

items.title: Top Firms
items.text: KPMG, PwC, EY, and local firms like TK & Partners, AM Law Firm handle M&A.

heroData.title: Software Development in Armenia
heroData.subtitle: Silicon Mountain Hub
heroData.description: Access world-class software development and IT services.

items.title: Major Players
items.text: Home to unicorns like Picsart and ServiceTitan. Global hubs for NVIDIA, Adobe, Synopsys.

items.title: Expertise
items.text: Strong in AI/ML, chip design, SaaS, and mobile app development.

items.title: Growth
items.text: Sector achieved $2.3B turnover in 2024. Gov aiming for deep tech leadership.

items.title: CodeRiders
items.text: Highly rated web/mobile agency.

items.title: Flux Technologies
items.text: Specialists in custom software and startup support.

items.title: AIST Global
items.text: Known for web and CMS solutions.

steps.title: Vendor Search
steps.description: Check Clutch.co listings for Armenia. Many firms specialize in Western markets.

steps.title: Contracting
steps.description: Contracts are usually Service Agreements. IP transfer is standard.

steps.title: Project Kickoff
steps.description: Agile methodologies are standard. Time zone (GMT+4) works well with EU/Asia.

items.title: Senior Developers
items.text: $3,000 - $5,000+ USD per month. High demand for AI/ML specialists.

items.title: Junior/Mid
items.text: $1,000 - $2,500 USD per month. Rapid salary growth (8-12% annual in 2025).

items.title: Retention
items.text: Benefits packages (gym, insurance, training) are critical. 60% income tax reimbursement (2025) for hiring foreign specialists is a major incentive.

faqs.question: What are hourly rates?
faqs.answer: Junior devs: $20-$30/hr. Senior/Architects: $40-$80/hr. Significantly lower than US/EU.

faqs.question: Is English common?
faqs.answer: Yes, English is the primary language of the IT sector.

heroData.title: Marketing Agencies in Armenia
heroData.subtitle: Digital & Creative
heroData.description: Full-service digital marketing, branding, and SEO agencies.

items.title: Publicis Armenia
items.text: Part of global network, full-service advertising.

items.title: Deem Communications
items.text: Strong in PR, events, and creative.

items.title: Prodigi
items.text: Digital-first agency dealing with SMM and performance.

items.title: Zuck Agency
items.text: Known for creative social media campaigns.

items.title: Social Media
items.text: Facebook and Instagram are dominant. LinkedIn growing for B2B.

items.title: SEO
items.text: Google is the primary search engine (~95% share). Content localization to Armenian is important for local B2C.

steps.title: Briefing
steps.description: Define target audience. Local cultural nuances are important.

steps.title: Localization
steps.description: Even if targeting English speakers, local language ads perform better for mass market.

steps.title: Launch
steps.description: Digital ad spend is tax-deductible expense.

faqs.question: Are there restrictions on ads?
faqs.answer: Yes, strict rules on alcohol, tobacco, and gambling advertising.
